newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BOLDON ACHIEVES AIM OF GETTING PICTURE IN PAPERS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BOLDON ACHIEVES AIM OF GETTING PICTURE IN PAPERS.

text.p: Trinidad's Ato Boldon achieved his goal of getting his name in the history books and his picture in the newspapers when he destroyed a high-class men's 200 metres field to win his first major title on Friday.

The Olympic bronze medallist, disappointed at finishing fifth in the 100 metres after complaining of muscle problems in his legs, came off the bend in front and stretched his lead over the last 100 metres to win by some five metres in 20.04 seconds.
The 23-year-old sprinter was not satisfied with the time but the gold medal put him exactly where he wanted to be.

"I didn't run as fast as I wanted to but I just decided to put my head down and give everybody a photo of me," he said. "I wanted to give the people something they would remember. I want to succeed in sport. I want to be the future of sport."

Boldon could afford himself the luxury of raising his arms in triumph as he crossed the line ahead of Namibia's former world champion Frankie Fredericks, who took the silver for the second consecutive championships in 20.23. Brazilian Claudinei Da Silva was third in 20.26.
In the crucial first part of the race Boldon got away well, ran an almost perfect bend and never looked in danger of being beaten once he hit the start of the home straight in front.
"This is the hardest thing I have had to do to date. I have been humbled by this world championship experience," he said. "It was mostly guts. I had run out of leg power. It was a mental check."

Apart from his victory at the 1993 championships in Stuttgart, Fredericks has had to settle for silver medals over 200 metres at most major championships -- the 1992 and 1996 Olympics Games and the 1991 and 1995 world championships.
But Boldon said he had been inspired by the day the Namibian ran the most successful race of his life in Stuttgart.
"Four years ago I asked Frankie if he could show me how to run 200 metres like that and get my name on a shoe," he said.

Fredericks, who has so often had to stand in the shadow of American 200 and 400 metres Olympic champion Michael Johnson who was not competing in the shorter event here, said he was not disappointed by his performance.

"I'm pretty happy with this silver medal. I have quite a lot of them and I'd like to change the colour, " he said. "I ran a bad turn and I realised that I couldn't catch him. Then I panicked and tried to hold on for silver, Ato was so far ahead."
